verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission features the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion is the spacecraft part of NASA's new rocket called the Space Launch System (SLS).'; R2: 'The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule'; R3: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) moon rocket'; R4: 'Space Launch System rocket...Orion capsule'; R5: 'Rocket: Space Launch System...Spacecraft: Orion'; R6: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket will propel the crewed Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state that Artemis II uses SLS rocket and Orion capsule.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will reach speeds of approximately 24,500 mph (39,430 km/h) to achieve escape velocity for the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The system [SLS] will power the Orion spacecraft to reach a speed of about 24,500 mph.'; R3: 'Escape velocity—or the speed Artemis II will achieve to free itself of the orbital pull of the Earth—is 24,500 miles per hour'; R6: 'Launch Speed Up to Mach 33 (24,500 mph or 39,430 kph)'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm ~24,500 mph for Earth's escape/translunar injection, not 'for the Moon' (Moon's escape velocity is ~5,300 mph); misattribution makes claim incorrect.

verifications.claim: During reentry, the Orion capsule will hit the atmosphere at about 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h) to test the heat shield.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '25,000 mph: Speed during Earth reentry'; R3: 'the spacecraft will reach a reentry speed of 25,000'; R4: 'top speed of 40,000 kph (25,000 mph). The spacecraft’s heat shield'; R5: 're-entered Earth's atmosphere at a maximum velocity of about 24,664 miles per hour'; R7: 'plunging into the atmosphere at speeds of about 25,000 mph...test the capsule's heat shield during reentry'
verifications.reasoning: References directly support reentry speed ~25,000 mph and heat shield testing.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket will push Orion to speeds exceeding 17,000 mph to reach Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph'; R3: 'Speeding along at 17,500 miles per hour—or 4.9 miles per second—the ship needs just 90 minutes to complete one full...orbit'; R8: 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm SLS achieves ~17,000-17,500 mph to enter Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: Orion will accelerate to over 24,500 mph for the trans-lunar injection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The system [SLS] will power the Orion spacecraft to reach a speed of about 24,500 mph'; R3: 'translunar injection (TLI)...Escape velocity...24,500 miles per hour'; R5: 'Orion performed a...TLI burn...to depart Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: References link ~24,500 mph to TLI/escape velocity achieved via Orion's engine post-SLS.

verifications.claim: During the trans-lunar coast, gravity will slow the spacecraft to approximately 3,400 mph during the journey to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'planetary gravity steadily pulling the ship backwards until it has slowed to just 3,400 mph. It is only when the ship is about 41,000 miles from the moon'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly describes gravity slowing spacecraft to 3,400 mph during trans-lunar coast.

verifications.claim: According to Boeing and USA Today, the Orion capsule will reach 25,000 mph (roughly Mach 33) upon returning to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2/R8 (USA Today): '25,000 mph: Speed during Earth reentry' (no Mach 33); R6 (Boeing): 'Launch Speed Up to Mach 33 (24,500 mph or 39,430 kph)'
verifications.reasoning: USA Today supports 25,000 mph reentry but not Mach 33; Boeing attributes Mach 33/24,500 mph to launch, not return; incorrect attribution and speed mismatch.

verifications.claim: As described by BBC and Sky at Night Magazine, parachutes will slow the capsule to approximately 17 mph for a safe landing in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4 (Sky): 'parachutes to slow the Orion capsule down to 17mph for splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'settle into the waters of the Pacific Ocean at a gentle 15 mph'
verifications.reasoning: R4 (Sky) directly supports 17 mph parachutes/Pacific splashdown; R3 supports similar speed/location (no BBC in sources, but fact clearly supported).

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make a 10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test mission'; R2: '10-day journey around the moon'; R3: '10-day journey around the far side of the moon'; R4: '10-day journey that will take them round the Moon'; R5: 'Mission duration9 days, 1 hour'; R6: 'Mission Duration 10 days'; R7: '10-day expedition around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm ~10-day mission around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit in over 50 years
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first humans in over 50 years — since Apollo 17 in December 1972 — to travel beyond low Earth orbit'; R3: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R4: 'first crewed flight of NASA's Artemis programme...beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo'; R5: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R7: 'first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'; R8: 'first humans in over 50 years — since Apollo 17 in December 1972 — to travel beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly state first crewed flight beyond LEO in >50 years since Apollo 17.
